newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Danish strike forces SAS to re-route cargo.
newsitem.headline: Danish strike forces SAS to re-route cargo.

text.p: SAS Cargo on Thursday said it was re-routing some cargo through airports in Paris and London because of the Danish truckers' strike, now in its fourth day.

Erik Lundqvist, spokesman at Scandinavian Airlines System's cargo unit, said it was also shipping some cargo on flights within Scandinavia to avoid Danish seaports and borders, which were blocked because of the industrial action.
"We are doing what we can to find ways to make sure the urgent shipments get in and out of Denmark," Lundqvist said.
"As a consequence we are operating very full inter- Scandinavian flights," he told Reuters.

Since SAS operated mostly smaller McDonnel Douglas MD-80s around Europe, freight which could only be loaded onto wide-bodied aircraft had to be routed to larger hub airports from which larger planes flew, Lundqvist said.
SAS trucks were not affected by the strike itself, but the vehicles were stopped at Danish borders, Lundqvist said.
He declined to say how much the strike was costing the airline, but said the alternatives were more expensive.
"It's a more costly option for our point of view because it requires more handling for the cargo,"
Danish truckers voted on Thursday to continue their protest against government plans to cut drivers' overseas subsistence allowances.
